shared_elements: human or anthropomorphic head/face in profile
relief carving in low/high relief on stone surface
justification: Both surfaces include an anthropomorphic face rendered in relief with schematic features and areas of crosshatched grid infill, which is the only reasonably specific correspondence; A also shows a large three-dimensional figure with an upturned head and blocky limbs, while B is a flat panel filled with a regular grid of many small square glyph-like signs in rows and columns. The organising principle differs completely: a single sculptural body versus a repetitive columnar array of small compartmentalised motifs, so arrangement and relationships share almost nothing.
